staged_readme:
# BM1397 programmed control state 501

Status: source staged for review. No build or original probe has run.
Production remains unchanged during common freeze499.

The next step adds `ControlWriteSupport::RegisterStorage` to the existing
`IdentificationChain`. Its normal constructor retains the former strict
capability. The explicit capability adds a bounded bank for each existing
chip. Addressing, power, reset, ticket filters, clock-order storage and packet
decoding continue through the same model. There is no second device model.

The new bank stores the posted core0 data byte and PLL0/PLL3 words. Core writes
must match the original T17 packing form. Other core registers, unsupported
forms, core reads, PLL reads, status and jobs remain errors. No write emits a
reply. Ambiguous addressed writes fail before any chip changes. Valid writes
with no selected chip leave every bank unchanged. Repeated writes update the
same state and have no one-shot bypass.

Reset or power loss removes knowledge of all three values. Each returns to
`None`, not a guessed silicon value. Access to this diagnostic state is
separate from guest readback. A written PLL bit31 is never treated as observed
lock. Internal core fan-out, clock polarity, completion and physical timing
remain unknown. This work does not establish a working ASIC or mining path.

The production arithmetic view follows original oracle496. Its regression
compares all22,134 results against the retained original output, including
the four results below the rational floor. Zero divisors return an explicit
error. Raw register storage does not reject or repair an invalid physical
configuration; the model makes no effective-clock claim for it.

The explicit `bm1397-control-storage-adc` probe selects this capability and
excludes the earlier one-shot observer. It retains the existing one-chip,
power, reset, ADC and UART fixture assumptions. Its profile, model source hash
and programmed state changes are recorded. All original-board and mining
gates remain false. The expected next unknown command is register0x28, the
fast UART configuration. That is a source prediction until actual execution.

Evidence:

- Original T17 packing oracle272/274 fixes the core0 command format.
- Original formatter472 fixes field extraction, not core effects.
- Exact archived ESP driver `9bd28dff43cb3c07a63c4843dba2704f7e071b1bfc7fb310cfd925cb35be2f56`
  posts core0, ticket, PLL3, fast UART and baud commands without a completion read.
- Original factory probe036 reaches the PLL3 write after the separate observer.
- Original arithmetic oracle496 and its independent review prove the direct
  divisor arithmetic. New source493 has conflicts and is not used to infer
  lock or reset defaults.

Next: root source review, exact base-hash check, integration after499 capture,
focused tests/Clippy/release, then a fresh original factory probe. Keep failed
traces and unknown commands explicit. No lower deadline, filter override or
fabricated return value is part of this change.
